lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to understand your situation. 

**Do you have a child (or children) you're claiming for?** If yes, could you tell me:
1. **How old is your child?** (or if you have multiple children, please provide their ages)
2. **What are their names?** (This will help me keep track as we go through the assessment)

This is important because Child Benefit eligibility depends on the age of the child:
- Children **under 16** may automatically qualify
- Young people **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Those **20 or over** are generally not eligible

Please share your child's/children's details, and I'll guide you through the rest of the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do have a child I'd like to claim for. His name is Alex and he's 16 years old. He lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have Alex, who is 16 years old and lives with you at home.

Since Alex is 16, he falls into the age category where eligibility depends on whether he's in approved education or training. Let me check the next step in the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to understand Alex's current situation regarding education or training.

**Which of the following applies to Alex?**

1. **He is currently in approved education or training** (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs, or other approved courses)

2. **He recently left education or training** (within the last few months)

3. **Neither** - he's not in education/training and hasn't recently left

Please let me know which situation applies to Alex, and I'll continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is currently in education - he's studying for his A-levels.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is studying for his A-levels, he's in approved education. Now I need to check that the level of education meets the requirements for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! A-levels are approved education for Child Benefit purposes. Now I need to verify a few details about Alex's course to make sure it meets all the requirements:

**Questions about Alex's A-level studies:**

1. **Is the course full-time?** (at least 12 hours per week of supervised study - this typically includes lessons, tutorials, and supervised coursework)

2. **Is Alex working at all?** If yes, how many hours per week does he work?

3. **Is Alex married or in a civil partnership?**

These details are important because:
- The education must be full-time (12+ hours/week of supervised study)
- If he works, we need to ensure it's not considered full-time work
- Marital status can affect eligibility for 16-19 year olds

Please let me know these details about Alex's situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's a full-time course at sixth form college - he's there every weekday. He doesn't have a job, so no work hours at all. And no, he's not married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's very helpful. So to summarize Alex's situation:
- Full-time A-level course at sixth form college ✓
- Not working ✓
- Not married ✓

This means Alex is in approved non-advanced education. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is not working at all (0 hours), he definitely meets this requirement - he's working less than 24 hours per week. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about benefits:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right?** Specifically:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Or similar benefits claimed in his own name

Most 16-year-olds in full-time education don't receive these benefits, but I need to confirm this for Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a student living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's good to know. Since Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name, we can continue. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex doing an apprenticeship?**

You mentioned he's studying A-levels at sixth form college, which sounds like traditional education rather than an apprenticeship, but I need to confirm this because:
- Most apprenticeships in England and Scotland would disqualify him from Child Benefit
- Only Foundation Apprenticeships in Wales are approved

Can you confirm that Alex is NOT doing any type of apprenticeship - he's just doing regular A-levels?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, he's just doing regular A-levels at sixth form - not an apprenticeship at all.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is doing regular A-levels and not an apprenticeship, we can continue. Let me move to the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now we need to check your residency status. This is about where **you** (the claimant) normally live.

**Do any of these apply to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common situation)

2. **You have settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme

3. **You have pre-settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme (and meet additional conditions like working, studying, or having sufficient resources)

4. **You're a Crown servant** living abroad

Most people claiming Child Benefit simply live in the UK normally. **Do you normally live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since you normally live in the UK (in Manchester), you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to confirm responsibility for Alex. You mentioned earlier that Alex lives at home with you, which means you meet this requirement. 

**To confirm: Alex lives with you in Manchester, correct?**

This shows you have responsibility for him. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex lives at home with me here in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex lives with you, you clearly have responsibility for him. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another guardian or relative
- Anyone else

If there is someone else claiming, we'd need to determine if they're willing to transfer the claim to you, or if there's a dispute about who should claim.

**Is there anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or are you the only person claiming/intending to claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. I'm the only one.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, we can continue. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation. You mentioned he lives at home with you, but I need to confirm there are no special circumstances:

**Does any of the following apply to Alex?**

1. **In hospital** - Is Alex currently staying in hospital?
2. **In care** - Is Alex in local authority care?
3. **Fostered** - Is Alex being fostered?
4. **None of the above** - Alex is living normally at home with you

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like option 4 (living normally at home), but please confirm which applies.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: None of the above - Alex is just living normally at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex is living normally at home with you, let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Just one final check:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

Since Alex lives at home with you in Manchester and is just a regular student, I expect the answer is no - the council is not paying for him. But I need to confirm this.

**Can you confirm that the local council is NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance costs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. He just lives at home with me and I support him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Since the council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance, let me move to the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

Based on the information you've provided, **you meet all the eligibility requirements** for Child Benefit for Alex.

### Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex qualifies as a child** - He's 16 and in approved full-time education (A-levels)  
✅ **Approved education** - A-levels are non-advanced, approved education  
✅ **Not working full-time** - Alex isn't working at all  
✅ **No disqualifying benefits** - Alex doesn't receive benefits in his own right  
✅ **Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship** - He's doing regular A-levels  
✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You live in the UK (Manchester)  
✅ **You have responsibility** - Alex lives at home with you  
✅ **No competing claims** - Nobody else is claiming for Alex  
✅ **Normal living situation** - Alex lives at home normally  
✅ **No council support** - The council isn't paying towards Alex's costs

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay some or all of it back through your tax return
5. **Payments** are typically made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

You can apply here: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

**Important note about Alex's age:** Remember that Child Benefit for 16-19 year olds continues only while they remain in approved education or training. If Alex leaves education, you must notify HMRC.

Do you have any questions about the application process?

The claimant normally lives in the UK (Manchester), has responsibility for Alex as he lives at home with them, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, he is living normally at home (not in hospital, care, or fostered), and the local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria are met.
